purpose: Caspofungin is used to treat serious fungal infections in the body, including infections in the blood, lungs, and other organs. It is often used for people whose immune systems are weakened, such as cancer patients or transplant recipients. It can also be used when other antifungal medicines have not worked.
how_it_works: Caspofungin works by attacking the outer wall of the fungus, called the cell wall, which humans do not have. It blocks a key building block the fungus needs to keep its wall strong and intact. Without a strong cell wall, the fungus falls apart and dies, helping your body fight off the infection.
common_side_effects: Fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, flushing or redness of the skin, and swelling or pain at the injection site. Some people may also notice changes in lab results like liver enzyme levels, which your doctor will monitor.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as the dose may need to be adjusted. Let your healthcare team know about all medicines you take, because caspofungin can interact with other drugs like cyclosporine, tacrolimus, or rifampin. Rarely, serious allergic reactions including rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing can occur — seek help immediately if this happens. This medicine is given by IV in a hospital or clinic, so it will always be given under medical supervision.
typical_dosing: Caspofungin is given once a day through an IV (directly into a vein) by a nurse or healthcare provider. A common starting dose for adults is 70 mg on the first day, followed by 50 mg once daily after that. Your doctor will decide the exact dose based on your weight, the type of infection, and how your liver is working.
